title: Holdout Vector Registry and Body-Scope Firewall
objective: Separate Earth/Terra candidates from vectors reported for other planets or stars: build a sealed holdout vector registry with train/dev/holdout partitions, enforce train/holdout disjointness, keep sealed fit anchors out of the holdout set, type foreign bodies out of scope (never force-decoded), and reference every vector by an opaque public id.

repository_truth.head: de620bb
reused_engine: cwatlas.r1082.geocode_forward.BODY_IN_SCOPE (Earth/Terra scope); cwatlas.r1082.source_import.STONEHENGE_FIXTURE_ID; cwatlas.r1082.spatialization route constants; cwatlas.r1082.claims - NOT reimplemented

claims.statement: A source vector registry splits vectors into sealed train/dev/holdout partitions; a vector cannot appear in two partitions (train/holdout disjointness), the two sealed T05 fit anchors may never be registered as holdouts, foreign-body vectors are typed out of scope and routed to FOREIGN (not force-decoded onto Earth), and every vector is referenced by an opaque public id; the holdout partition is sealed with a deterministic SHA-256 digest.

negative_results: A vector reported for MARS or a star that shares the 01|65 prefix with Stonehenge is NOT force-decoded onto Earth: it is typed FOREIGN_OUT_OF_SCOPE and excluded from the Earth-root partitions.
Registering the same opaque id into both training and holdout is refused; the train and holdout id sets are provably disjoint.
A sealed calibration anchor (Wilkes fixed root or the Stonehenge training anchor) is refused as a holdout - a fit anchor is not an unseen holdout.
Registration stores only an opaque id, the sanitised route shape, and a route hash; no raw private vector or narrative is ever stored or exported.
privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic/public opaque-id fixtures only; no private path literals, no personal identity tokens, no raw private vectors or narrative
